subject: Feature Request: Keyword to Hide Output when Printing

messages.author: 8c4f70ab584cd6d9
messages.subject: Feature Request: Keyword to Hide Output when Printing
parts:
I often find that when I am using transformed parameters that are very large, I do not always wish to see them in the plot or print calls in rstan. Plot will usually truncate to only show the first few variables, but if you print a fit that includes a vector transformed parameter with 1000+ entries, you may not even be able to scroll back up to the original parameters. Given the various ways of using Stan, I think a keyword allowing the user to specify the parameters (or transformed parameters or generated quantities) to hide when using plot or print would give the most flexibility. The use of it would be something like

     hide vector[N] Y;

or

     nodisplay vector[N] Y;

or

     someotherkeyword vector[N] Y;

It might also be helpful if there is an ability to toggle this on and off, like with the verbose option when calling the stan function.

messages.author: 5fe2aa3904fed17c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Feature Request: Keyword to Hide Output when Printing
parts:
Hi John,

If you're using R, you can accomplish that using the "pars" argument in plot, print, and other methods.

e.g.

print(mdl, pars = c("a", "b")) # This only prints the summary of "a" and "b"

or

# This prints the summary of all parameters except "a" and "b"
print(mdl, pars = m@sim$pars_oi[!m@sim$pars_oi %in% c("y_rep")])

You can also specify the parameters you want using pars in the sampling and stan functions, which can be useful when you are generating lots of quantities that may take up too much memory like saving the log_lik, or replications per iteration

Hope that helps,
Juan Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Feature Request: Keyword to Hide Output when Printing
parts:
I believe the term of art is "nuisance".

Here are three ways to get rid of them.

Let's suppose you have transformed parameter alpha to
save and beta not to save.

transformed parameters {
real alpha;
real beta;
... define alpha and beta ...
...
}

0. As Juan Sebastián Casallas pointed out, you can
suppress the output from R.

1. If you don't need beta to compute alpha, it makes
most sense to make it a local variable in the model.

transformed parameters {
real alpha;
... define alpha ...
...
model {
real beta;
... define beta ...
...
}

The local variables in a model (including everything declared
at the top, are not printed.

2. The more general approach is to define beta as a local
within the transformed parameters block.

transformed parameters {
real alpha;
{
real beta; // local variable, won't be printed
... define alpha and beta
}
...
}

But that won't work if you actually need beta in the model
block. You need 1 for that. But 1 won't always work,
because sometimes you need beta to define alpha efficiently.

- Bob

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Feature Request: Keyword to Hide Output when Printing
parts:
For the R functions, maybe a wrapper for print would be cool where the user could supply with_pars or without_pars (not both I guess, as that would be confusing) instead of just pars to make it easier to exclude a few parameters. A quick, crude, way of doing it would be 


stan_print <- function(x, with_pars, without_pars, ...) {
  wp <- !missing(with_pars)
  wop <- !missing(without_pars)
  
  if (wp & wop) stop("Specify only one of 'with_pars' and 'without_pars'")
  if (!(wp | wop)) return(print(x, ...))
  if (wp) return(print(x, pars = with_pars, ...))
  else print(x, pars = x@sim$pars_oi[!x@sim$pars_oi %in% without_pars], ...)
}

So then stan_print(stanfit) does the default print(stanfit), stan_print(stanfit, with_pars = c("a", "b")) does print(stanfit, pars = c("a", "b")) and stan_print(stanfit, without_pars = c("a","b")) does what Juan suggested for removing parameters from the output.

transformed parameters {
  real keep;
  {
    vector exclude;
    ...
    keep <- f(exclude);
  }
}
